scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: HELP! The workstation it_lab3 (one of the IT lab
machines on 192.168.1.x) has turned into a complete BRICK. It can't reach
anything at all, not even its own gateway thing. Its port on the lab switch
has obviously DIED -- the machine is fine, the hole it plugs into is dead,
I'd bet money on it!! Please swap it_lab3 onto a working port (or turn its
port back on) and make it talk to the network again!! The student who uses it
is just sitting there!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — `it_lab3` unable to reach its own gateway or anything else — is not reproducible and no fault exists in the lab. Every layer of the network affecting `it_lab3` was inspected and found healthy.

At the physical/link layer, `it_lab3`'s `eth0` is UP/LOWER_UP (carrier present), and both ports on `switch0` (the IT-LAN bridge) are also UP and forwarding normally. The switch port is not dead. At the IP layer, `it_lab3` holds the correct address `192.168.1.5/24` with a valid default route to the gateway `192.168.1.1` (`router0.eth0`). This matches the configuration of every other IT-LAN host (`it_hod` through `it_lab4`). Live ping tests from `it_lab3` confirmed zero packet loss to the gateway (1 hop), a same-segment peer (`it_lab1`, 0% loss), a cross-subnet host (`cs_hod` on 192.168.2.x, 0% loss), and a remote multi-hop host (`pc1` on 1.0.0.5, 0% loss). `router0` carries a complete RIP routing table covering all subnets in the topology. There are no iptables rules blocking traffic on `it_lab3`.

The ticket's claim of a dead switch port is incorrect. The network is functioning normally. No corrective action is required; the student or a prior observer may have experienced a transient condition (e.g., momentary ARP resolution delay at startup) that self-resolved, or the report was simply mistaken.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states it_lab3 has 192.168.1.5/24 and confirms 0% packet loss to its gateway 192.168.1.1.
